text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Palestinian President Arafat briefs King Hussein in phone call on course of talks in Taba between PLO and Israel.
- Information Minister Muasher says construction of Israeli settlements complicates Middle East peace process.
- King Hussein attends graduation of special royal guard cadets.
- Iraqi trade minister says trade relations with Jordan are "good and continuing".
- General Professional Unions' council announces its solidarity with sit-in planned for Saturday by engineering unions.
- Jordanian-British military manoeuvres held east of Qatranah desert.
- Jordan buys 150,000 tonnes of wheat at $164.94 per tonne in three lots for November, December and January delivery.
- Libya says visit of King Hussein to Jericho "is a brave position and a challenge to Israel."
- Egypt's Foreign Minister says his country shares Jordan's position over events in northern Iraq and says two countries continuously coordinate their stances on develoments there.
- Doctors' union to hold general assembly meeting on Friday to discuss pay issues and social security and pension fund for employees.
